(Remote, US East Coast or the same time zone. Series B. DevTools SaaS. Synthetic monitoring. 40h/week)
The best developers don’t wait for a customer to tell them something’s broken.
They catch it first, in the pull request, in staging, or in the checkout flow at 3am, before a single user notices. That instinct is Checkly’s whole reason to exist. Now that agents write and ship more and more code, they can carry that instinct too. Agents write, run, and maintain the monitoring setup that guards production, while developers stay in control. Everything is defined as code, powered by OpenTelemetry and Playwright, and versioned and reviewed like everything else that ships. From pull request to post-mortem, in one place.
AI agents are shipping more code than any team can review, and reliability is lagging behind. Checkly closes this gap. As a Support Engineer, you’ll support our most valuable customers, from modern AI companies like Mistral and resolve.ai to large engineering orgs like LinkedIn, Citi, and 1Password on that journey.
In 2024 we raised $20M in Series B funding from Balderton, CRV and Accel. We’re a remote-first startup that is low on meetings, high on productivity, and always shipping. If you love actually listening to and working with customers, working async, and keeping it lean, you’ll fit right in!
We care about building a team where people of all backgrounds are encouraged to do their best work. To achieve this we built a flexible and async-first startup environment with inclusive benefits and full transparency about how we pay.
## What you’ll do
Support has always been about solving real problems for real people. What’s changing at Checkly is how we do it: AI lets us automate routine work and assist us with troubleshooting, so we can go deeper on hard cases and bring what customers tell us straight back to the product. Here’s where you come in:
• Resolve customer issues. Debug Playwright tests (flaky selectors, timeouts, auth flows). Dig into API check failures with packet captures (PCAPs), traceroutes and timing breakdowns. Set up single sign-on (SSO) and SAML. When it’s a bug, bring engineering a clean reproduction, or open the pull request (PR) yourself.
• Build an outstanding AI support process. Our internal and external support agents already resolve 80% of tickets. You’ll help lift the bar: what the agent answers, when it hands off to a human, and how good those answers are.
• Turn tickets into product. Spot patterns across customers and bring product and engineering a reproduction. Your work becomes bug fixes and features.
• Own the docs. If you’ve answered something twice, it belongs in the docs and in the agent, so customers and AI get the same right answer.
• Work with modern tooling. We are continuously updating our workbench, and you’ll have modern tools like Plain, Linear, and Mintlify.
## This won't be the right role if you...
• Want a clear process for every situation before you act.
• Would rather code all day than talk to customers.
• See AI tools as something you’ll get around to eventually.
• Want the structure and pace of a large company.
## What you should have
You will often speak with developers who need assistance understanding if their applications work well and if not, what caused the issue. This requires a solid technical background and a genuine motivation to help and learn.
• Empathy: You love working with customers and solving their problems. Checkly is critical to them, and we genuinely want to unblock them.
• Some experience in a technical role, for example, as a developer or in technical support.
• You can read and debug JavaScript, TypeScript and Node.js code.
• You’re comfortable with HTTP, REST APIs, browser dev tools, git and CI/CD practices.
• AI is already how you work. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or similar are part of your day. You’ve built your own workflows.
• You write and speak clear, friendly English.
• You can run your own day remotely and still enjoy working with your team.
• You're based on the US East Coast or the same time zone.
## Why us?
• Transparent salary because your salary shouldn't be dictated by how good a negotiator you are. (more info below)
• Async-first (low meeting, high productivity) and transparent culture
• Stock options
• Flexible paid vacation
• Paid sick leave & up to 14 weeks of paid parental leave
• US: Medical, Dental, Vision, FSA, long- and short-term disability, life insurance, 401(k) and more
• Annual company off-site
Find out more here .
## What we pay
Fair, competitive, and transparent pay is very important for us. Therefore we work with a standardized salary calculator that includes several factors such as seniority level as well as location.
For this role, the range is
• $57,500 - $70,000 for someone in the US
• $71,910 - $87,000 for someone in US Tier 1 locations like NYC, Boston

Teams are shipping faster than their test data can keep up, and that gap is our business.

About the Role
mpathic provides independent, multidisciplinary evaluations of healthcare AI technologies seeking deployment in real-world clinical settings. As part of our work supporting Utah's Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy (OAIP) regulatory sandbox, we are recruiting experienced machine learning (ML) and data science professionals to serve as technical reviewers on expert evaluation panels.
In this role, you will independently assess the technical evidence supporting healthcare AI applications, including model performance, validation methodology, generalizability, reliability, and proposed monitoring and safeguards. Your assessments will help inform recommendations regarding whether and under what conditions an AI technology may be appropriate for pilot deployment.
You will work alongside clinical and other subject-matter experts to evaluate whether applicants' technical claims are supported by credible evidence and whether their proposed evaluation and monitoring plans are appropriate for the intended healthcare setting and patient population.
This is an evaluation and scientific review role, not a model development position. We are looking for experts who can critically assess existing evidence, identify limitations, and communicate actionable recommendations to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
What You'll Be Doing
Responsibilities may include:
• Evaluate model performance and validation: Assess the appropriateness of validation methods, reference standards, sample sizes, statistical analyses, performance metrics, operating thresholds, and reported uncertainty.
• Assess data quality and representativeness: Review whether training, testing, and validation datasets are appropriate for the intended clinical application, including potential data leakage, subgroup performance differences, and generalizability across patient populations and healthcare settings.
• Evaluate technical reliability: Assess evidence of model robustness, reproducibility, known failure modes, and performance under atypical or out-of-distribution inputs.
• Review proposed evaluation plans: Determine whether applicants have established scientifically defensible methods, performance benchmarks, and success criteria for evaluating AI technologies during pilot deployment, particularly when pre-deployment evidence is limited.
• Assess technical safeguards and human oversight: Evaluate whether proposed technical safeguards, escalation mechanisms, and human-in-the-loop processes are operationally feasible and supported by appropriate testing.
• Evaluate monitoring and change management: Assess applicants' plans for detecting performance degradation, monitoring model behavior, managing updates, and establishing criteria for intervention or rollback.
• Collaborate with multidisciplinary reviewers: Work alongside clinicians and other technical experts to identify concerns that require cross-disciplinary judgment, particularly where model performance may affect clinical outcomes.
• Produce structured evaluation findings: Document strengths, limitations, missing evidence, and technical concerns using a standardized review framework. Provide clear, evidence-based recommendations and identify what additional evidence or changes would resolve identified concerns.
• Participate in reviewer calibration and quality assurance: Contribute to discussions intended to improve consistency, transparency, and defensibility across evaluations.
• Maintain independence and confidentiality: Follow conflict-of-interest, confidentiality, and data-handling requirements when reviewing proprietary or unpublished materials.
What We're Looking For
We are seeking technically rigorous, independent reviewers who can distinguish between a promising technology and evidence that adequately supports its proposed use.
Strong candidates are comfortable questioning unsupported performance claims, identifying limitations in study design, and recognizing when additional evidence is needed before meaningful conclusions can be drawn. They understand that healthcare AI evaluation is context-dependent: technical performance must be considered alongside the intended population, clinical application, degree of autonomy, and potential consequences of model error.
Candidates should also be able to translate complex technical findings into clear, actionable recommendations for multidisciplinary audiences, including clinicians and state regulatory stakeholders.
Basic Qualifications
• At least 3 years of professional or applied research experience in machine learning, data science, biostatistics, clinical informatics, or a closely related field, with direct experience evaluating or validating predictive models or AI systems.
• Demonstrated understanding of model evaluation methodologies, including appropriate performance metrics, validation design, statistical uncertainty, threshold selection, and common sources of bias or methodological error.
• Experience assessing model performance on independent or held-out data and interpreting whether reported performance generalizes beyond the evaluation dataset.
• Hands-on experience evaluating at least one relevant class of AI systems, such as clinical natural language processing, large language models, conversational AI, medical imaging, computer vision, or tabular predictive models.
• Ability to critically assess technical research, evaluation reports, or validation studies and identify methodological limitations or unsupported conclusions.
• Strong analytical writing skills, including the ability to communicate complex findings clearly to non-technical audiences.
• Ability to work independently while contributing to multidisciplinary expert review and calibration processes.
• Willingness to complete confidentiality agreements, conflict-of-interest disclosures, and reviewer training requirements.
Preferred Qualifications

## About Skylight
Skylight is a digital consultancy using design and technology to help government agencies deliver better public services.
We’re at the forefront of a civic movement to reinvent how all levels of government serve families, patients, and many others in today’s digital world.
If you want to play a part in driving this critical movement forward, we’d love for you to join our growing team of public interest technologists.
The work we do matters.
## About the job
At Skylight, software engineers design, implement, and maintain software systems to improve government services for users. This software is built to meet the needs of regular users of government services as well as Skylight’s partners in government.
Skylight is partnering with a U.S. Air Force program office that runs a portfolio of civil engineering systems. These systems serve users across civil engineering, security forces, and services, including readiness managers, range personnel, and fire and emergency services. Releases are slow today. Regression testing is manual, security review happens after development finishes, and code freeze to production can take a month or more. We’ll move the program to an outcome-driven model with test automation and security built into the pipeline, starting with migrating the first application onto a DoD software factory. Leadership wants this office to become the model other Air Force offices adopt.
In this role, you’ll own test strategy across the portfolio and lead the move from manual to automated regression, so the team can ship with confidence and say clearly when a release is ready.

Your first 30 days are about working with the Skylight team and government personnel, learning how the program office gets changes to users today, and understanding where testing and security slow things down. This is new work that replaces a traditional support model, so part of the job is coaching your government partners to keep these practices running after we leave. Expect to work alongside government engineers and other contractors, with tools and processes changing as the work gets underway.
This role is contingent on Skylight being awarded the underlying contract. If we’re not awarded the contract, we’ll let you know promptly and discuss whether there are other opportunities that fit.

• Design the test strategy for a portfolio of web applications, and decide pragmatically what to automate first
• Build automated regression suites and integrate them into the CI/CD pipeline
• Move the team from manual to automated regression testing, shrinking the time from code freeze to production

• Communicate release confidence clearly to non-technical stakeholders

Europe

Head of Engineering Platform
Squad embedding
Embedded and active in one squad - not a standalone QA manager
Chapter scope
Platform: 4 Squads (4–6 embedded QA engineers)
About Watu
Watu is a fintech company operating across Africa and Latin America, providing device financing and financial services to customers historically excluded from the formal financial system. We finance motorcycles, smartphones and other productive assets through a technology-first, data-driven approach - enabling customers to own income-generating assets and build credit histories.
Our platform supports millions of customer journeys across Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Ivory Coast, Ghana, and beyond, with continued expansion into LATAM.
The Role
The QA Chapter Lead is a senior QA engineer who carries two roles simultaneously. First, you are an embedded QA engineer in one of the squads - attending ceremonies, writing automated tests, defining acceptance criteria, and owning the Definition of Done for your squad. Second, you are the QA Chapter Lead for your engineering function, responsible for QA standards, tooling, automation frameworks, and test strategy across all squads in the function.
You report to the Head of Engineering - not to a Tech Lead. This reporting line is intentional: it gives you the organisational standing to influence QA practice across squads you are not embedded in, and it ensures the Head of Engineering actively drives QA strategy rather than delegating it entirely to individual Tech Leads.
This is not a QA manager role. There is no QA team to manage. There is a chapter of QA engineers across squads, and you are their technical lead and standards-setter - not their line manager. The QA Guild (monthly cross-chapter meeting with the counterpart Chapter Lead from the other engineering function) is your primary mechanism for cross-function consistency.
What You Will Own
As embedded QA engineer in your squad
Attend all squad ceremonies - sprint planning, daily standup, sprint review, retrospective. QA is in the room from the start, not brought in at the end.
Define acceptance criteria with the Product Owner before each sprint. Stories without clear acceptance criteria do not enter the sprint.
Write and maintain automated test suites for your squad's domain - unit, integration, E2E as appropriate. Test coverage is your responsibility.
Own the squad's Definition of Done quality gate - nothing ships without passing the criteria you have defined and maintained.
As QA Chapter Lead across your function
Define and maintain QA standards for the function: test pyramid structure, automation tooling, naming conventions, coverage thresholds, and CI gate configuration.
Onboard new QA engineers into the chapter - they join a squad, but they join your standards. Define the onboarding process and the baseline expectations.
Run the monthly QA Guild with the counterpart Chapter Lead from the other engineering function. Alignment on tooling, shared frameworks, and Definition of Done consistency across the full engineering organization.
Own the automation framework selection and evolution - evaluate new tooling, deprecate old, and maintain documentation that any QA engineer can follow.
Report to the Head of Engineering on QA chapter health: coverage trends, flaky test rates, automation backlog, and any systemic quality issues.
Who You Are
Essential
5+ years of software QA experience with at least 2 years in a Lead QA role where you drove test strategy across more than one team.
Strong automation engineering skills - you write test code to a production standard. Your test suites are maintainable, readable, and run reliably in CI.
Experience with API testing at depth: REST, contract testing, integration test design. Most of Watu's QA surface area is backend and API-level.
Experience defining and maintaining QA standards in an Agile squad environment - not as a gatekeeper at the end of a sprint, but as an embedded contributor from day one.
Experience in Java-based backend environments - you can read Java code, understand the architecture, and write tests that reflect it accurately.
Strongly preferred
Experience in fintech, payments, or digital financial services - you understand what it means to test systems that move money.
Experience with performance and load testing - understanding payment rail throughput, API concurrency limits, and how to surface them before production does.
Mobile app testing experience is mandatory for one of the QA Chapter roles (Android surface).
Experience building or evolving a QA chapter, guild, or community of practice across multiple teams.
Familiarity with AI-assisted test generation tooling - test case generation, regression triage, and synthetic test data creation using LLMs.

Design, build and maintain useful unit and component tests for SDK behaviour.

Turn repeated investigation or testing work into reusable AI workflows, tools, checks or test assets.

What Good Looks Like

Important SDK behaviours have dependable automated protection;
Useful quality improvements land incrementally and are easy for the team to adopt;
SDK-to-platform integration failures are detected early and are easy to diagnose;
Tests run reliably in the workflows the team actually uses;

We are looking for an early-career systems engineer who likes figuring out what a system actually needs to do and then proving that it does. You’ll sit down with the operators who use DoD mission systems every day, turn what they tell you into clear, testable requirements, and write the test procedures that operators and developers use to verify each release. Just as important, you’ll explain why a request should or shouldn’t be built, and stand behind that recommendation. Our purpose is singular — to optimize warfighter performance
through information technology.
We hire for talent and drive over years on a résumé. Strong recent graduates are encouraged to apply.
You have…
• A clear, structured voice. You can walk someone through a problem — the situation, the options you weighed, what you decided, and the result so operators, engineers, and leaders follow it the first time.
• A curious mind. You want to understand how a system is really used, not just how it was designed.
• A good ear and good judgment. You listen for what operators need versus what they ask for, weigh it against technical constraints and the backlog, and can tell a customer “not now” while pointing them to a better path.
• An ownership mindset. When something is blocked, you go find the person who can unblock it instead of waiting.
• A dedication to detail. A vague requirement becomes a bug or a dispute later, so you pin it down now.
• A focus on the craft. You want to go deep in systems engineering and software requirements, test, and how software actually gets built.
• An open mind. You welcome feedback on your work and want to grow as an engineer.
We have…
• A devotion to making technology work for the warfighter. We help operators work faster, better, and smarter.
• An affinity to action. We’d rather start, learn, and iterate than wait for the perfect plan.

Requirements elicitation and decomposition

• Trace requirements across subsystems and interfaces (APIs, data exchanges, connected systems) and assess the ripple effect of each change.
• Capture non-functional requirements (the “-ilities”): performance, reliability, security, and operation in degraded or disconnected (DDIL) conditions.

• Capture every operator or customer request as a data point: log it in the backlog, link it to existing requirements, and track it to a decision.

• Close the loop with operators on what was decided and when.
Documentation

• Write user stories with measurable acceptance criteria, including Given-When-Then (Gherkin) scenarios.

• Execute and support functional, regression, integration, and user acceptance testing (UAT) for software releases.
• Record results, log defects with clear reproduction steps, and verify fixes.
• Help automate repeatable testing: write simple scripts for test data and log checks, turn manual procedures into automated test cases and BDD step definitions.
• Contribute to functional security test cases (authentication, access control).

## About Practifi (The Real Story)
Practifi is the only intelligent CRM company that meets wealth management firms wherever they are in their AI adoption journey. Our enterprise-grade, compliance-first foundation brings client data, workflows, and relationship intelligence together in one system, so firms can understand what matters, take the right action, and scale without ever needing a new CRM.
That same directness runs through how we work. We're a team of fewer than 100 people, remote-first across the US and Australia, and we'd rather tell you how this job actually works than polish it for the pitch. We don't sell a version of the role that doesn't exist.
## The Opportunity (What This Role Really Means)
When a wealth management firm moves onto Practifi, the first thing they judge us on is their data. If a household is missing a member, if a client shows up twice, or if a servicing team points to the wrong advisor, they notice on day one. So do their clients.
Right now, quality assurance on those data migrations is handled by whoever is delivering the engagement, on top of everything else on their plate. It works, but it means every client gets a slightly different process and nobody has a clear view of the issues that keep coming back.
We're creating this role to change that. As our Data QA Analyst, you'll be the dedicated owner of data migration quality across every client onboarding engagement. You'll work the checklist object by object, build one standard the whole team uses, and spot the patterns a single-project view misses. You'll be a big part of why a client's first login feels like their business, not a spreadsheet import.
## Your Day-to-Day (The Honest Version)
The Core Work
• Validate every migration end to end. You'll analyze source data (record counts, missing values, duplicates, orphaned contacts, inconsistent values), then walk through the Practifi interface object by object to confirm everything displays and connects the way the client's Data Mapping Document says it should.
• Check the details that matter. Every record carries a valid External Id and Batch Id, nothing is owned by a default system user, every contact is tied to at least one relationship, and counts reconcile to source or have a clear explanation.
• Log, route, and retest. You'll capture screenshots of failed checks, log findings in Asana and JIRA, route fixes to engineering, and retest once they're corrected.
• Report clearly. After each Initial Load and Final Load, you'll give the Project Manager, Consultant, or Business Analyst the metrics they need, and you'll prepare the final QA sign-off report before go-live.
• Raise the flag early. When a data issue puts a go-live at risk, you'll escalate it to the Project Manager within 24 hours
• Build the standard. You'll own one QA checklist and issue-tracking format for every engagement, replacing the client-by-client workbooks in use today, and you'll track recurring issues across clients so we fix the process, not just the record.
The Reality Check
The Practifi data model has its own vocabulary, and it takes time to learn how it all fits together. You won't figure it out alone. You'll complete the same onboarding and training curriculum as every individual contributor here, including our PractifiU learning platform, and you'll have a Practibuddy mentor from day one.
You'll also be working alongside Consultants, Business and Data Analysts, Data Engineers, and Project Managers. Part of the job is raising problems in a way that keeps projects moving. And when QA volume is lighter, you'll flex into delivery support, so you'll see the whole implementation, not just your portion of it.
The Growth
This is a new role, which means you'll shape it. The checklist, the reporting format, and the process improvements you contribute each quarter become part of how Data Services operates.
You'll earn a Salesforce certification once you're here, with time and support built in, and an annual Learnbucks stipend for the courses and certifications you choose after that. We promote from within. A role that sees every engagement is a strong foundation for a path into consulting, data engineering, or delivery leadership.
## What We're Really Looking For
The Must-Haves
• 3 to 5 years of experience in data quality, data migration, data validation, or quality assurance, ideally in a CRM or software environment
• Hands-on experience reconciling data: comparing record counts, running field-by-field checks, and finding duplicate and orphaned records
• Comfort working inside Salesforce or a comparable CRM, navigating objects, records, and related lists
• A working understanding of how relational data fits together (IDs, lookups, and records that link other records)
• Experience logging and tracking issues in JIRA, Asana, or a similar tool
• Clear written communication, including findings a non-technical stakeholder can act on
The Nice-to-Haves
• Experience with Salesforce Inspector, the Salesforce Developer Console, Data Loader, or SOQL queries
• Background in wealth management, financial services, or another regulated industry
• Experience supporting client onboarding or software implementation projects
• Strong spreadsheet skills (lookups, pivot tables, conditional formatting)
A Salesforce certification isn't required to apply. You'll earn one with us.
The More Important Stuff
• You’re observant and tuned into the details within the data.
• You care about the cause of an issue, not just the fix.
• You're comfortable telling a Project Manager something they don't want to hear, and you do it early and kindly.
• You like building structure where there isn't any yet.
• You're honest about what you don't know and curious enough to go find out.
## What Taking This Leap Gets You
The Practical Stuff
• Base salary: $78,000 to $95,000. We share the range because you deserve to know it before you apply. Where you land depends on your experience against the role.
• Generous time off: 20 days of paid vacation, 10 sick days, 3 personal days, and 3 volunteering days annually
• Medical, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance benefits, plus a 401(k) with company match
• Fully remote within the US
The Cultural Stuff
• A Practibuddy mentor from your first day, so you always have someone to ask
• An annual Learnbucks education stipend for the courses and certifications you choose
• Bi-annual in-person summits in Chicago where the whole company gets together
• A Slack culture where questions are welcome and wins get celebrated
• Remote-first that's real: genuine work-life integration, not a line in a job ad
## Living Our Values Daily
• Growth: You'll be part of building a function from the ground up, with Learnbucks and a real promotion path behind you.
• Collaboration: You'll partner with every delivery role on every engagement, and the fix is always a team effort.
• Transparency: The salary is in this ad, and your QA findings will be shared openly, good news and bad.

We are seeking a senior, hands-on Performance Engineering Sr. QA Manager (M3) to lead a Performance Engineering Center of Excellence and own QA delivery for a product portfolio supporting high-transaction healthcare platforms. This role is ideal for a technical leader who can improve the reliability, scalability, and performance of EMR/EHR systems while mentoring strong QA teams and influencing engineering decisions with data. The candidate will shape performance strategy, build realistic workload models, diagnose complex bottlenecks, leverage observability, guide tooling architecture, and strengthen QA processes, quality metrics, and release readiness across systems built on microservices, APIs, cloud-native platforms, and modern frontend architectures.
## Key Responsibilities
• Lead the Performance Engineering CoE by defining performance standards, reusable frameworks, tooling strategy, governance practices, and enablement models that scale across product lines.

• Lead release readiness and QA governance reviews with clear entry and exit criteria, test strategy alignment, go/no-go recommendations, defect triage discipline, test evidence, release process adherence, and transparent risk communication.
• Improve QA productivity by reducing test cycle time, increasing defect detection efficiency, improving MTTR, strengthening sprint predictability, stabilizing environments, and reducing flaky automation.
• Partner with product, engineering, architecture, DevOps, and QA leaders during planning, design reviews, defect triage, release readiness, and product discussions to surface risks early and influence decisions with data.

• Ability to program and script in Java, Groovy, Python, or equivalent languages to build test scripts, utilities, custom extensions, and automation support.
• Strong working knowledge of modern distributed architectures, including microservices, APIs, API gateways, event-driven systems, containers, Java Spring Boot services, and React-based frontend or micro-frontend applications.
• Experience integrating quality and performance validation into CI/CD pipelines using Jenkins, GitLab CI, Azure DevOps, or equivalent platforms, with automated execution, pipeline reporting, performance gates, and release thresholds.
• Strong understanding of system performance tuning across JVM internals, garbage collection, thread analysis, connection pools, application server configuration, OS and infrastructure utilization, and autoscaling behavior.
• Practical experience with Dynatrace or comparable APM tools, distributed tracing, dashboards, alerting, proactive monitoring, and performance analysis across Oracle, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, query tuning, and indexing.
• Strong troubleshooting capability across application code, JVM, database, network, infrastructure, and frontend layers, with the ability to translate findings into actionable engineering recommendations.
